drivers.label: Wireline revenue as a share of the AI-cluster Ethernet optics market
drivers.source: Market: LightCounting (CY2025 ~$16.5B via POET 20-F, src 14; growth +120% 2026, +76% 2027, src 12/13). Wireline revenue: KEYS does not disclose it; Q3 FY26 remarks (src 11): wireline exceeded wireless in Q3 of CC $1,006M; Q4 FY26 CFO (src 2): triple-digit wireline growth, CC $1,145M.
drivers.derivation: Wireline FY26 quarters are estimates (not disclosed): 358/428/520/645 = 1,951; Q4 645 = +108% on the Q4 FY25 estimate 310 (CFO: triple-digit), leaving wireless 500 of CC 1,145 (src 1, 2). FY wireline growth = 1/3 x optics market growth (manufacturing test scales with module units) + 2/3 x R&D test spend growth (estimate +20% FY27, +10% FY28, +8% FY29: 1.6T ramp and 3.2T in R&D per CEO, src 2): FY27 1/3 x 76% + 2/3 x 20% = +38.7% -> 2,706; FY28 market +45% (judgment, between LightCounting's +76% 2027 and +20% 2031, src 12, below the straight-line +62% because rule 0c leans conservative) -> 1/3 x 45% + 2/3 x 10% = +21.7% -> 3,293; FY29 market +30% -> 1/3 x 30% + 2/3 x 8% = +15.3% -> 3,797. FY n paired with CY n. Market quarters: each CY split at a constant within-year quarterly growth rate. Wireline quarters within a year grow at one quarterly rate from Q4 FY26 645 so the yearly build totals hold; capture = wireline / market (5.4% FY26 -> 4.3% FY27 -> 3.5% FY28 -> 3.1% FY29). Evidence-based alternatives: (a) LightCounting straight-line market path (+62% 2028, +48% 2029) gives wireline FY28 ~3,416 and FY29 ~4,150; (b) Q4 FY26 run-rate x4 = 2,580 for FY27 (no growth through FY27) despite record orders and book-to-bill 1.17 (src 1); (c) CEO's 20% total-company base case (src 2) would put wireline near 3,000 if other lines are as built.
drivers.why: Wireline test demand is driven by AI optical interconnect build-outs and speed transitions; LightCounting's market forecast is the outside series, capture maps it into KEYS revenue.

drivers.label: Wireless revenue (commercial communications ex wireline)
